First, we recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{3\pi }{2}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 0-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-1) \\  & =1\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+0\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
